mainTopic: Establishing שביתה from a distance, whether an עירוב gives ארבע אמות, and the man who set out and was turned back (saying vs. setting out)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story. רבה בר רב חנן used to declare his Shabbat residence at צינתא from home. אביי challenges him from רב נחמן's view, which a ברייתא supports, and רבה בר רב חנן retracts. רמי בר חמא then asks whether someone who places an עירוב of bread gets ארבע אמות, like someone who stands at the spot in person. רבא tries to prove that he does, but the proof is rejected. A new משנה follows: a man set out toward another town and his friend turned him back. רבי יהודה lets him go there on Shabbat but forbids the other townspeople, while רבי מאיר calls him a חמר גמל. רב הונא explains that the man has two houses, so once he sets out he counts as an עני, while the others are עשירים. רבה and רב יוסף disagree about what רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue over: saying the declaration or actually setting out. עולא's ruling is shown to follow רב יוסף, and a story about רב נתן בר אושעיא and his guest shows the rule in practice.

steps.title: רבה בר רב חנן declares his residence in צינתא
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן would say from home: 'Let my Shabbat residence be in צינתא.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say: 'Let my Shabbat residence be in צינתא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes describing what רבה בר רב חנן used to do. He declared his Shabbat residence at צינתא, a spot between two towns, while he was still at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually you set your residence either by physically standing there or by placing an עירוב of food there. He did neither. He only spoke the words from a distance. That is why his practice needs a justification.

keyTerms.meaning: Shabbat residence; the point from which your 2000 אמות are measured
Tzinta, a settlement between the Shabbat boundaries of two towns

phrases.english: He would say: 'Let my Shabbat residence be in Tzinta.'
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבה בר רב חנן, from the end of the previous daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, רבה בר רב חנן set his שביתה at a distant spot by words alone.

steps.title: אביי asks what reasoning רבה בר רב חנן relies on
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests the basis. The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and רב חסדא says their dispute is about saying 'in such-and-such place.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is your reasoning? Is it that in a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and רב חסדא said the dispute is about one who said 'in such-and-such place'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks רבה בר רב חנן what his practice is based on, and offers the likely answer himself. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two building blocks. First, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה against רבי מאיר. Second, according to רב חסדא, רבי יהודה allows a declaration of 'such-and-such place' even without being there. Putting these together seems to justify what רבה בר רב חנן did.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows רבי יהודה

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: What is your reasoning?
In a dispute of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda,
the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rav Chisda said:
the dispute is where he said 'in such-and-such place.'
phrases.notes: According to רב חסדא, רבי יהודה accepts this kind of declaration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Probes the basis for the practice described in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The halachic basis for declaring שביתה from a distance.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Proposed basis: הלכה כרבי יהודה, combined with רב חסדא's version of the dispute.

steps.title: Challenge from רב נחמן, supported by a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: But רב נחמן explained the dispute differently, and a ברייתא supports him!
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is רב נחמן, and a ברייתא was taught in accordance with him!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the reasoning he just laid out. רב נחמן gives a different version of the dispute, and a ברייתא backs רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן, the dispute is about someone who said 'at its base' (בעיקרו). If someone said 'in such-and-such place,' everyone agrees it does not work. So even following רבי יהודה, רבה בר רב חנן's declaration fails. And since a ברייתא supports רב נחמן, his version is stronger than רב חסדא's.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in support of him

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the הלכה follows רבי מאיר. He agrees the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. The question is only what exactly רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר argued about.

phrases.english: But there is Rav Nachman,
phrases.notes: He holds that 'such-and-such place' fails according to everyone.

phrases.english: and a baraita was taught in accordance with him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the רב חסדא premise offered in Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: Relying on רב חסדא's version of the dispute.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן's version, which a ברייתא supports, makes 'such-and-such place' invalid according to everyone.

steps.title: רבה בר רב חנן retracts
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן admits the challenge and says: 'I retract.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I retract.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב חנן accepts אביי's challenge and drops his practice. This ends the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא supports רב נחמן, declaring 'such-and-such place' from a distance does not work. רבה בר רב חנן therefore stops doing it.

keyTerms.meaning: I retract; I take back my position

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion follows רב נחמן. Declaring 'my residence is in such-and-such place' from a distance does not establish שביתה, even according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: He said to him: I retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concedes the קשיא of Step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practice is abandoned; רב נחמן's version is accepted.

steps.title: Does one who places an עירוב get ארבע אמות?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks a new question. One who acquires residence by standing somewhere gets ארבע אמות; does one who places an עירוב get them too?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: They have said that one who acquires residence [by being there] has ארבע אמות. One who places his עירוב: does he have ארבע אמות, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רמי בר חמא asks whether an עירוב made with food gives the same ארבע אמות bonus as being physically present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person standing in a spot acquires ארבע אמות around himself, plus 2000 אמות beyond that. The doubt is whether an עירוב of food, which works in place of the person, gets this extra space too.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, a person's personal space
Or not? (marks a question with two sides)

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ שָׁבַת יֵשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: They have said: one who acquired residence has four cubits.
One who places his eruv,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: does he have four cubits, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, unrelated to the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an עירוב of food grants ארבע אמות like physical presence does.

steps.title: רבא quotes the rule that a bread עירוב is a leniency for the rich
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the source: an עירוב with bread was allowed only as a leniency for the wealthy man, so he need not go out on foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, come and hear: They only said one may make an עירוב with bread to be lenient with the wealthy person, so that he need not go out and make the עירוב with his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source to answer רמי בר חמא. This step only quotes the source; the reasoning comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source says the bread עירוב was meant as an easier option. A wealthy person can send bread instead of walking there himself. This sets up the comparison between the two methods.

keyTerms.meaning: One makes an עירוב with bread
To be lenient; to make things easier
With his feet (by going there in person)

phrases.english: Rava said, come and hear:
They only said one makes an eruv with bread
to be lenient with the wealthy person,
so that he need not go out and make the eruv with his feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to resolve the question of Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That one who places an עירוב has ארבע אמות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'לא אמרו מערבין בפת אלא להקל על העשיר'.

steps.title: Without ארבע אמות, the bread עירוב would be a stringency
steps.stepSummary: If the bread עירוב gave no ארבע אמות, it would be worse than walking, which is a stringency and not a leniency. So it must give ארבע אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he does not have [ארבע אמות], is this a leniency? It is a stringency!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws the conclusion from the source. A bread עירוב must give at least as much as walking there, so it also gives ארבע אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something called a 'leniency' cannot leave a person worse off. If the bread עירוב lost the ארבע אמות that walking gives, it would be a stringency. So the two methods must be equal, and one who places an עירוב also has ארבע אמות.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof tries to show that an עירוב of bread is equal to establishing residence by foot, so one who places an עירוב would also get ארבע אמות. The next step rejects this proof, so do not treat it as the conclusion.

phrases.english: And if you say he does not have [four cubits],
is this a leniency?!
It is a stringency!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the source quoted in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: One who places an עירוב has ארבע אמות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'להקל' in the משנה cannot fit a version where the bread עירוב gives less than walking does.

steps.title: The wealthy man may want bread even without four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Even if a bread עירוב gives no ארבע אמות, the wealthy man is still happy with it, because it saves him the walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, he is pleased with it, so that he does not have to bother himself and go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רבא's proof from the bread עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא argued that a bread עירוב must give ארבע אמות. Otherwise it would be worse than walking, and the רבנן called it a leniency. The answer is that saving the effort of walking out is already a big benefit. So it counts as a leniency even if he loses the ארבע אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: It is pleasing / preferable to him
He will exert himself, take the trouble

steps.whatToRemember: The proof is rejected, so רמי בר חמא's question about whether an עירוב gives ארבע אמות is left without a proof here.

phrases.english: Even so, it is preferable to him,
phrases.notes: Meaning: even if he loses the four cubits.

phrases.english: so that he need not exert himself and go out.
phrases.notes: The real benefit is skipping the walk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the bread עירוב being called a leniency for the wealthy man.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the only possible benefit was ארבע אמות. Saving the effort of walking is a benefit by itself.

steps.title: משנה: the man who set out and was turned back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules on a man who set out on ערב שבת toward another town to set up his Shabbos boundary there, but his friend turned him back. He himself may go to that town on Shabbos, but the other townspeople may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person set out to walk toward a town that people normally reach on Shabbos by making an עירוב, and his friend made him turn back. He is permitted to go there, but all the other people of the town are forbidden. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a new case. A man set out on foot to establish his Shabbos residence toward another town, but never finished the trip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you must actually reach the spot, or place food there, to move your Shabbos boundary. רבי יהודה says that setting out on the trip already helps this man. It does not help the other townspeople who never set out. The גמרא will soon ask why he is different from them.

keyTerms.meaning: A town people normally reach on Shabbos by making an עירוב
And his friend made him turn back

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
phrases.notes: Start of a new משנה.

phrases.english: One who set out to go
phrases.notes: On ערב שבת, on foot.

phrases.english: to a town for which people make an eruv,
phrases.notes: A town reached on Shabbos only by extending the boundary.

phrases.english: and his friend made him return —
phrases.notes: He never finished the trip.

phrases.english: he is permitted to go,
phrases.notes: To that town on Shabbos.

phrases.english: and all the people of the town are forbidden,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehudah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיָּצָא לֵילֵךְ בְּעִיר שֶׁמְּעָרְבִין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the man who set out and was turned back may go to the town. The other townspeople may not.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: like a donkey driver and camel driver
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says that whoever could have made an עירוב but did not is like a חמר גמל, pulled in two directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Anyone who could make an עירוב and did not is like a donkey driver and camel driver.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives his own view on the same kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donkey driver walks behind his animal, and a camel driver walks in front of his. A person who is both is pulled two ways. Here, the person's residence is unclear. It might be at home, or at the spot along the road. So he is limited by both possibilities and may only walk where the two boundaries overlap.

keyTerms.meaning: A donkey driver and camel driver, someone pulled in two directions

steps.confusionAlert: חמר גמל is a comparison, not a real case about animals. It means the person gets the restrictions of both possible residences, not the benefits of either.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לְעָרֵב וְלֹא עֵירַב —
phrases.english: Anyone who is able to make an eruv and did not make an eruv —
phrases.notes: He gave up his home residence but never clearly set a new one.

phrases.english: he is a donkey driver and camel driver.
phrases.notes: He is restricted by both possible boundaries.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לְעָרֵב וְלֹא עֵירַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion in the same משנה, disagreeing with רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who could have made an עירוב but did not is restricted by both possible residences, like a חמר גמל.

steps.title: Why is he different from everyone else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, according to רבי יהודה, the man who set out may go, while the other townspeople may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about him, and what is different about them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the reason behind רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה. This question sets up רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the end, neither he nor the others reached the spot or placed an עירוב. So why should he be allowed and they forbidden? The גמרא wants to know what makes his situation special.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Start of the גמרא on this משנה.

phrases.english: What is different about him
and what is different about them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא אִיהוּ וּמַאי שְׁנָא אִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי יהודה's ruling from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the difference between the man who set out and the other townspeople?

steps.title: רב הונא: he has two houses far apart
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the משנה is talking about a man who has two houses, one in each town, with two Shabbos boundaries (4000 אמות) between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Here we are dealing with a case where he has two houses, and between them is the distance of two Shabbos boundaries.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא starts answering by defining the exact case of the משנה. The full explanation of why this helps will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man is not an ordinary traveler. He has a home in each town. That special setup is what will separate him from the other townspeople. The distance of 4000 אמות means the halfway point is exactly 2000 אמות from each house.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (introduces a specific case)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
With what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: He narrows the משנה to a specific case.

phrases.english: For example, where he has two houses,
phrases.notes: One in each town.

phrases.english: and between them is two Shabbos boundaries.
phrases.notes: 4000 אמות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 by defining the case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The man has two houses, 4000 אמות apart. This special case sets him apart from the other townspeople.

steps.title: The traveler counts as a poor man, the townspeople as wealthy
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא finishes his answer. The man who set out counts as an עני, so he can set up his Shabbos spot without food. The other townspeople count as עשירים and cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He, since he already set out on his way, is treated like a poor man. But these other people are treated like wealthy people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב הונא's answer to the question of why only the traveler may go to the other town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עני (someone stuck on the road with no food at hand) is allowed to set up his Shabbos spot just by declaring it, without placing food there. Once the man started walking toward his other house, he got this status. The townspeople are sitting at home with food, so they are עשירים, and they can only do it by putting real food at the spot before Shabbos.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'poor man.' Here it means someone on the road who may set up his Shabbos spot just by declaring it.
'Wealthy people.' Here it means people at home with food, who must put down food to make an עירוב.
He went out onto the road (he set out).

steps.confusionAlert: עני and עשיר here have nothing to do with money. They describe whether a person is at home with food (עשיר) or out on the road (עני) when it comes to making an עירוב.

phrases.english: He, since he went out on the road,
phrases.notes: The man who set out on ערב שבת toward his other house.

phrases.english: he is considered a poor man.
phrases.notes: So he can set up his Shabbos spot just by declaring it.

phrases.english: But these others are wealthy people.
phrases.notes: The townspeople at home need a food עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's answer begun in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the traveler may go while the townspeople may not (step 11).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Setting out on the road gave him the status of an עני, who can acquire a Shabbos spot by declaring it. The townspeople are עשירים who need real food.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this: setting out on the road is enough
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a man with two houses 4000 אמות apart acquires an עירוב once he sets out on the road. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: someone who has two houses with two Shabbos boundaries between them acquires an עירוב once he sets out on the road. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב הונא's explanation exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes the same case רב הונא described: two houses, two תחומין apart. It rules that setting out on the road is enough to acquire the Shabbos spot, even with no food placed there. That fits the idea that the traveler counts as an עני.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught this way.' A ברייתא that supports what was just said.
He set out on the road (he actually started walking).
He acquired an עירוב (his Shabbos home base is set).

phrases.english: It was also taught so in a baraita:
One who has two houses,
and between them is the distance of two Shabbos boundaries,
phrases.notes: 4000 אמות.

phrases.english: once he has set out on the road,
he has acquired an eruv. These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting רב הונא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's explanation that the traveler with two houses acquires his Shabbos spot by setting out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה about a man with two houses two תחומין apart.

steps.title: Even a man stopped before leaving may go the next morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה goes further. Even if a friend convinced him to stay overnight because of the heat or cold, he may get up early on Shabbos and go.
steps.simpleTranslation: Going even further, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: even if his friend found him and told him, 'Sleep here, it's a hot season' or 'it's a cold season,' tomorrow he may get up early and go.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a broader opinion from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is more lenient than רבי יהודה: even if a friend talked him into staying overnight, he may go the next morning. Exactly what רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is lenient about is debated in the next two steps. According to רבה, he does not require setting out at all. According to רב יוסף, both require setting out, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not require saying it out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Even more than that.' Introduces a more far-reaching opinion.
A hot season / a cold season (bad weather for traveling).
He gets up early and goes.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Even more than this, Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda said:
Even if his friend found him and said to him:
phrases.notes: Whether this means before or after he set out depends on רבה vs. רב יוסף (next steps).

phrases.english: "Sleep over here,

phrases.aramaic: עֵת חַמָּה הוּא, עֵת צִינָּה הוּא״ —
phrases.english: it is a hot season, it is a cold season"
tomorrow he gets up early and goes.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a more lenient opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if a friend persuaded him to stay overnight, he may rise early and go to the other town on Shabbat morning.

steps.title: רבה explains the dispute: speaking is needed, walking is debated
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that both opinions agree the man must say out loud that his Shabbos spot is in the other place. They only argue about whether he must actually set out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: about saying it, everyone agrees he needs to. Where they argue is about setting out on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה steps in to define exactly what רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagree about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions require a spoken declaration of where his Shabbos spot is. Without it, his staying home could look like he changed his mind. The only argument is over physically starting the trip: רבי יהודה requires it, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says intention plus the declaration is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: To say (to declare where his Shabbos spot is).
To set out (actually start the trip).

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, both opinions require a spoken declaration. רבי יהודה also requires starting to walk, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not. רב יוסף disagrees with this reading in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives one way to define the minimum for the poor man's עירוב. רב יוסף offers the mirror-image definition in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabba said: regarding saying it,
everyone agrees that it is required;
where they argue is about setting out on the road.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לוֹמַר כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּצְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the point of dispute between the two opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A spoken declaration is required according to all. The dispute is only about whether he must physically set out.

steps.title: רב יוסף flips the dispute: setting out is required by all, and the argument is about saying
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says both תנאים agree the man must actually set out. They argue only about whether he must also say out loud where his Shabbos spot is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: Everyone agrees that he needs to set out. Where they argue is about whether he needs to say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different explanation of the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. His version is the opposite of רבה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said saying is required by everyone and setting out is the point of argument. רב יוסף says setting out is required by everyone and saying is the point of argument. In רב יוסף's version, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds the man does not need to say anything, since he already set out. רבי יהודה holds he also needs to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: To set out on the road (literally 'to take hold' of the way)
Everyone; both sides of the argument
To say out loud (that his Shabbos spot is over there)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה and רב יוסף. Their positions are mirror images. For רבה, everyone requires saying and the argument is about setting out. For רב יוסף, everyone requires setting out and the argument is about saying.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: לְהַחְזִיק — דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּצְרִיךְ,
phrases.english: Regarding setting out, everyone agrees that it is necessary;
where they disagree is about saying it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the reverse of רבה's explanation in Step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting out is required by all. The dispute is whether he must also say out loud where his Shabbos spot is.

steps.title: Whose view matches עולא's ruling about the man who was talked into returning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes עולא: a man who set out and was persuaded by his friend to go back is both 'returned' and 'set out.' It asks which opinion this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does עולא's statement follow? A man who set out on the road, and his friend got him to go back, is considered 'returned' and 'set out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from עולא and asks which version of the argument it fits. This sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that there are two versions of the מחלוקת, רבה's and רב יוסף's, the גמרא tests them against a known ruling. Before it can answer, it first has to understand what עולא's odd wording means.

keyTerms.meaning: His friend made him go back

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which Ulla said:
One who set out on the road
and his friend made him return,
he is considered returned and set out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב יוסף's and רבה's versions against עולא's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which version of the dispute, and which תנא, does עולא's ruling follow?

steps.title: עולא's wording seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא's words. 'Returned' and 'set out' seem to be opposites, so how can he be both?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is 'returned,' why is he 'set out'? And if he is 'set out,' why is he 'returned'?
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering whose view this is, the גמרא points out that עולא's own words do not seem to make sense together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Returned' sounds like he is just like the rest of the townspeople and has no Shabbos spot elsewhere. 'Set out' sounds like he did set up his Shabbos spot over there. Both cannot be true at once.

keyTerms.meaning: If this is so, why that? (shows two claims clash)

phrases.english: If he is returned, why is he set out?
And if he is set out, why is he returned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pauses the question of attribution to attack the wording of עולא's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of עולא's statement: 'מוחזר ומוחזק'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two terms are opposite legal statuses. A person cannot be both at the same time.

steps.title: עולא means: even though he went back, he still counts as having set out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads עולא's words to mean 'even though he was returned, he is still counted as set out.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Even though he was sent back, he still counts as having set out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of עולא's words so they no longer contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Returned' only describes what physically happened: he went back home. The legal ruling is that he still counts as 'set out,' so his Shabbos spot stays at the far place. Going back does not cancel his setting out.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a re-reading of the words)

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Even though he is returned, he is considered set out.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמּוּחְזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words seemed to claim two opposite statuses at once.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Returned' describes what physically happened. 'Set out' is the legal status, and it stays in force.

steps.title: עולא follows רב יוסף's version, according to רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its question: עולא follows רב יוסף's version of the argument, on the side of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? רב יוסף's, according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the question from Step 18 about whose view עולא's ruling follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In עולא's case the man actually set out, which רב יוסף says everyone requires. But עולא never says the man declared anything out loud. Under רב יוסף's version, it is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה who does not require saying, so עולא's ruling fits his side.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, everyone requires actually setting out, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not require saying it out loud. עולא's ruling follows this. Once a man has set out, his Shabbos spot stays at the far place even if his friend talks him into going back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the physical act of setting out is what counts. Being persuaded to go back afterward does not undo the man's Shabbos spot.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rav Yosef,
and according to Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the corrected reading from Step 20 to answer the question from Step 18
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולא's ruling follows רב יוסף's version, according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. Setting out is enough, and no spoken declaration is needed.

steps.title: A guest brings a basket of fruit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a story: רב יהודה בר אישתתא brought a basket of fruit to רב נתן בר אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר אישתתא brought a basket of fruit to רב נתן בר אושעיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a story that will show the rule we just learned being used in real life. This line only sets the scene.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One explanation is that this visit took place on ערב שבת, and the guest's home was 4,000 אמות away. That is twice the normal 2,000-אמה limit for walking on שבת, so getting home on שבת will be the problem the story solves.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Ishtata
brought a basket of fruit
to Rav Natan bar Oshaya.
phrases.notes: This was on ערב שבת, in a town 4,000 אמות from the guest's home.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אִישְׁתָּתָא אַיְיתִי לֵיהּ כַּלְכַּלָּה דְפֵירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that illustrates עולא's rule, which was just shown to follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This is a scene-setting line with no ruling yet. A guest visits a sage on ערב שבת, far from home.

steps.title: Letting him start, then inviting him to stay
steps.stepSummary: As the guest left, רב נתן waited until he went down one step and then told him to sleep over. The next morning the guest left early.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he was leaving, רב נתן let him go until he went down one step, and then said to him: Sleep here. The next day he got up early and went.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נתן deliberately let his guest actually begin his trip home, even by just one step, before inviting him to stay. The guest slept over and set off early the next morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going down that one step counts as 'setting out' toward home. By עולא's rule, being persuaded to come back does not cancel that. So his שבת spot counts as being out on the road toward home, and from there he may walk the rest of the way on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Even one real step on the way out counts as 'setting out.' Coming back afterward, because a friend persuaded you, does not undo it. This follows עולא and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נתן did not wait for a step by accident. He let the guest go down the step on purpose, so the guest would count as having set out before being invited back.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a sage relying on עולא's rule in practice. This supports the view that being 'returned' still counts as 'set out.'

phrases.english: When he was going,
he let him go until he went down one step,
phrases.notes: This step is what makes him count as having set out on his trip.

phrases.english: and said to him: Sleep here.
The next day he rose early and went,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה אָזֵיל, שַׁבְקֵיהּ עַד דִּנְחֵית דַּרְגָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and shows the actual practice: he sets out, is persuaded to come back, and still counts as having set out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, a man who takes even one step on his way and is then persuaded to stay still counts as having set out, so he may continue home on שבת.
